extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants, investors, accounting professionals, and commenters on SEC rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and implementation expectations related to the SEC's climate-related disclosure requirements (Regulation S-K/Regulation S-X), including thresholds, metric definitions, reporting periods, and presentation/aggregation rules for financial impacts and expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1% disclosure threshold for financial statement line items
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed threshold of 1% of the total line item (including for expenditure items) as the trigger for disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters disagreed: some supported the 1% threshold (e.g., ICGN, Sarasin), others opposed it as inconsistent with materiality law or burdensome. Some recommended alternative thresholds (e.g., ranges of 5–10% suggested by CEMEX; APCIA recommended 10%; AIC noted a $1 million threshold in Item 103 Reg S-K for certain disclosures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide commentary when investor interest makes impacts material even if below threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the aggregate impact is less than the 1% threshold, registrants should still be required to offer commentary when investors have expressed a clear interest in understanding the impact (thus making it material).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICGN and Sarasin recommended additional disclosure or commentary in such cases; this recognizes qualitative investor interest may make amounts material even if they fall below numeric bright lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not net positive and negative impacts when assessing disclosure triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: Positive and negative impacts should be considered separately, not netted, in determining whether a disclosure threshold is met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters (e.g., ICGN, MN SBI, Morningstar, PwC) cautioned that netting can hide large absolute impacts (e.g., insurance recoveries masking gross losses); absolute values aid investor understanding by distinguishing negative impacts from positive mitigation/opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disaggregate aggregated category impacts when a single identified risk meets threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Require a separate disclosure footnote to disaggregate any category impact if any single identified climate-related risk within an aggregated category was 1% or more of the total line item on its own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested by Dana Invest.; KPMG noted such an approach would be based on amounts recorded in the financial statements. This is an approach to preserve usefulness where aggregations would mask individual material impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive financial-impact disclosures from transactions and books and records
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of financial impacts from climate-related activities should be derived from transactions and amounts recorded in the books and records underlying the financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended by Ceres and echoed by other commenters; aligns disclosure to amounts actually recorded under U.S. GAAP and promotes defensibility and auditability of reported figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expenditure metrics focus on spending in each reported fiscal year(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expenditure metrics are focused on expenditures (spending) incurred in each reported fiscal year(s), and the number of periods of the expenditure metrics should correspond to the number of years of income statement or cash flow statement presented in the consolidated financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This links the scope and temporal granularity of expenditure metrics directly to the financial statement presentation periods. (Cites to proposed rules and Staff Accounting Bulletin provisions.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not adopt Financial Impact Metrics (as proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission is not adopting the proposed Financial Impact Metrics; registrants will not have the option to disclose the impact of climate-related opportunities on those Financial Impact Metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a result, requirements tied to proposed Rule 14-02(i) (including requiring inclusion of climate impacts on the Financial Impact Metrics) are not being adopted. The release states why the Commission declined to adopt those proposed metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider separate reporting thresholds for physical events and transition activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement reporting thresholds for physical events separately from reporting thresholds for transition activities and do not permit netting between them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encouraged by commenters (e.g., MN SBI) to avoid conflating distinct types of climate impacts and to prevent offsetting effects between different categories that would obscure material physical or transition impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer absolute values for investor usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: There is more value for investors in absolute numbers in this context; disclose gross losses and gains rather than netting to provide clearer insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BC IM Corp., Morningstar, PwC and others argued absolute values allow investors to distinguish negative impacts (severe weather, regulatory changes) from positive impacts (mitigation, resilience, opportunities). Example: insurance proceeds should not be netted against gross loss when assessing disclosure triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid requiring quantification of indirect impacts when operationally impracticable
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantifying the indirect impact of severe weather events on sales and cost of sales can be exceedingly difficult and require significant judgment, estimates, and assumptions, which may limit comparability and usefulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raised by Dow and others as an anti-pattern: regulators should be cautious about mandating indirect-impact quantifications that impose heavy judgment and reduce comparability across registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational feasibility: track specific costs incurred for climate-related impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be operationally possible for registrants to track specific costs incurred to mitigate transition risks or costs incurred due to severe weather events and natural conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters such as Crowe, Dow, and Nutrien noted operational capability exists for certain direct costs (e.g., costs to mitigate or recover from weather events), which supports disclosure tied to recorded transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose current period and planned capital expenditures attributable to climate risks/opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of current period and planned capital expenditures to show the portion of investments attributable to addressing transition risks and opportunities and adaptation to or mitigation of physical risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended by Ceres to provide investors visibility into CAPEX allocation for climate-related strategies and adaptations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align terminology and definitions between Regulation S-K and Regulation S-X
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission should align the terminology between the proposed rules under Regulation S-K and Regulation S-X to avoid inconsistency and confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested by Amazon and KPMG; alignment helps registrants prepare consistent disclosures across regimes and reduces implementation complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider expanding industry guides for sector-specific disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission should consider expanding its industry guides (e.g., for mining, bank holding companies, real estate limited partnerships, property-casualty insurance underwriters) to address industry-specific climate disclosure issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended by Ceres to provide more tailored guidance where existing codified guides (oil & gas, mining, bank and savings & loan) help clarify disclosure expectations for particular sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude specific weather events from 'physical climate-related risks' definitions for (re)insurers (optional carve-out)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend excluding specific weather events from the definition of physical climate-related risks for (re)insurers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RAA recommended this exclusion given the nature of insurance accounting and risk modelling; commenters raised definitional tailoring for particular industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow alternative presentation formats (e.g., expenditure table) as potentially more workable
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative presentations, such as the expenditure table included in Amazon's comment letter, may be a more workable approach to reporting certain climate-related expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C2ES described Amazon's expenditure table as a workable alternative; commenters proposed different presentation formats to balance usefulness and operational burden.
